title: A functor isomorphic, through covering-compatible equivalences, to a morphism of sites is one
statement: Let $\mathcal A,\mathcal B,\mathcal C,\mathcal D$ be sites [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology] (Stacks sites: categories with sets of covering families). Let $p:\mathcal A\to\mathcal C$ and $q:\mathcal B\to\mathcal D$ be equivalences of categories such that a family $\{X_a\to X\}_{a\in A}$ of morphisms of $\mathcal A$ with common target is a covering of $\mathcal A$ if and only if $\{p(X_a)\to p(X)\}_{a\in A}$ is a covering of $\mathcal C$, and likewise for $q$ (a family of $\mathcal B$ is a covering iff its image under $q$ is a covering of $\mathcal D$). Let $u:\mathcal C\to\mathcal D$ be a continuous functor which defines a morphism of sites $\mathcal D\to\mathcal C$ (i.e. $u_s$ on sheaves of sets is exact) [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology](3), and let $u':\mathcal A\to\mathcal B$ be a functor together with a natural isomorphism $q\circ u'\cong u\circ p$. Then $u'$ is continuous (Sites, Definition 00WV: it maps coverings to coverings, and for a covering $\{X_a\to X\}$ and a morphism $T\to X$ of $\mathcal A$ the canonical morphisms $u'(T\times_XX_a)\to u'(T)\times_{u'(X)}u'(X_a)$ are isomorphisms) and defines a morphism of sites $\mathcal B\to\mathcal A$ ($u'_s$ on sheaves of sets is exact). (Sketch, for the queue: an equivalence preserves and reflects fibre products and isomorphisms, and a covering family stays one after composing with isomorphisms (axioms (i), (ii) of 00VH), which gives continuity; $p$ and a quasi-inverse are continuous, so $\mathcal G\mapsto\mathcal G\circ p$ is an equivalence $\Sh(\mathcal C)\to\Sh(\mathcal A)$, likewise for $q$; then $u'^s\circ q^s\cong p^s\circ u^s$, so by uniqueness of left adjoints $u'_s$ is isomorphic to the composite of $u_s$ with equivalences, hence exact.)

proof.text: *Step 1 (the equivalences are morphisms of sites).* By [lem-weil-pbc-site-equivalence-is-morphism-of-sites], applied to $p:\mathcal A\to\mathcal C$, $p$ is continuous and defines a morphism of sites $\mathcal C\to\mathcal A$ ($p_s$ exact). Choose a quasi-inverse $q':\mathcal D\to\mathcal B$ of $q$ with a natural isomorphism $\eta:\mathrm{id}_{\mathcal B}\xrightarrow{\sim}q'\circ q$; by the same node applied to $q:\mathcal B\to\mathcal D$ (clauses (2), (4) for the quasi-inverse), $q'$ is continuous and defines a morphism of sites $\mathcal B\to\mathcal D$ ($q'_s$ exact).

source.place: written by an agent; notions of Definitions Tag 00VH (line 679), 00WV (line 2524), 00X1 (line 2687), Lemmas 00WW, 00WX, 03CB

proof.text: *Step 2 ($u'\cong q'\circ u\circ p$).* Let $\alpha:q\circ u'\xrightarrow{\sim}u\circ p$ be the given natural isomorphism and put $w=q'\circ u\circ p:\mathcal A\to\mathcal B$. Then $\theta=(q'\alpha)\circ(\eta u'):u'\to q'qu'\to q'up=w$, with components $\theta_X=q'(\alpha_X)\circ\eta_{u'(X)}$, is a natural isomorphism $u'\cong w$ (a composite of whiskerings of natural isomorphisms).

source.place: written by an agent; notions of Definitions Tag 00VH (line 679), 00WV (line 2524), 00X1 (line 2687), Lemmas 00WW, 00WX, 03CB

proof.text: *Step 3 ($w$ is continuous and defines a morphism of sites).* Apply [lem-weil-pbc-site-morphism-composition] (Sites, Lemma 03CB) with $\mathcal C_3=\mathcal A$, $\mathcal C_2=\mathcal C$, $\mathcal C_1=\mathcal D$, $v=p$ (Step 1) and $u$ (continuous with $u_s$ exact by hypothesis): $u\circ p:\mathcal A\to\mathcal D$ is continuous and $(u\circ p)_s$ is exact. Apply it again with $\mathcal C_3=\mathcal A$, $\mathcal C_2=\mathcal D$, $\mathcal C_1=\mathcal B$, $v=u\circ p$ and $q'$ in place of $u$ (Step 1): $w=q'\circ(u\circ p)$ is continuous, $w_s$ on sheaves of sets is exact, and $w^s=p^s u^s q'^s$.

*Step 4 ($u'$ is continuous).* Let $\{g_a:V_a\to V\}_{a\in I}$ be a covering of $\mathcal A$. (a) By Step 3 $\{w(g_a):w(V_a)\to w(V)\}$ is a covering of $\mathcal B$; by naturality of $\theta$ (Step 2), $w(g_a)\circ\theta_{V_a}=\theta_V\circ u'(g_a)$ with $\theta_{V_a}$, $\theta_V$ isomorphisms, so by [lem-weil-pbc-site-covering-isomorphic-family] (with $\varphi=\theta_V$, $\sigma_a=\theta_{V_a}$) $\{u'(g_a):u'(V_a)\to u'(V)\}$ is a covering of $\mathcal B$. (b) Let $T\to V$ be a morphism of $\mathcal A$ and $P=T\times_VV_a$ (it exists by axiom (iii) of 00VH). By Step 3 a fibre product $Q=w(T)\times_{w(V)}w(V_a)$ exists in $\mathcal B$ and the canonical $c_w:w(P)\to Q$ is an isomorphism. The cospans $u'(T)\to u'(V)\leftarrow u'(V_a)$ and $w(T)\to w(V)\leftarrow w(V_a)$ are isomorphic through $(\theta_T,\theta_V,\theta_{V_a})$ (naturality), so $Q$ with the projections composed with $\theta_T^{-1}$, $\theta_{V_a}^{-1}$ is a fibre product $u'(T)\times_{u'(V)}u'(V_a)$, and the canonical morphism $c_{u'}:u'(P)\to Q$ for $u'$ equals $c_w\circ\theta_P$ (both have projections $\theta_T^{-1}w(\mathrm{pr}_1)\theta_P=u'(\mathrm{pr}_1)$ and $\theta_{V_a}^{-1}w(\mathrm{pr}_2)\theta_P=u'(\mathrm{pr}_2)$), an isomorphism. Hence $u'$ satisfies (a), (b) of Definition 00WV [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology](3).

proof.text: *Step 5 ($u'^s\cong w^s$).* Since $u'$ and $w$ are continuous (Steps 3, 4), $u'^s\mathcal G=\mathcal G\circ u'$ and $w^s\mathcal G=\mathcal G\circ w$ are sheaves on $\mathcal A$ for every sheaf of sets (resp. abelian sheaf) $\mathcal G$ on $\mathcal B$ [lem-weil-pbc-site-continuous-pushforward-sheaf]. The maps $\mathcal G(\theta_X):\mathcal G(w(X))\to\mathcal G(u'(X))$ are bijections (group isomorphisms), natural in $X$ by naturality of $\theta$ and in $\mathcal G$ by naturality of morphisms of sheaves; so they form a natural isomorphism $\delta:w^s\xrightarrow{\sim}u'^s$ of functors from sheaves on $\mathcal B$ to sheaves on $\mathcal A$.

source.place: written by an agent; notions of Definitions Tag 00VH (line 679), 00WV (line 2524), 00X1 (line 2687), Lemmas 00WW, 00WX, 03CB

proof.text: *Step 6 ($u'_s\cong w_s$).* By [lem-weil-pbc-continuous-functor-sheaf-pullback-adjunction] (Sites, Lemma 00WX) $u'_s\dashv u'^s$ and $w_s\dashv w^s$ on sheaves of sets. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-conjugate-iso-unit-equation] with $L_1=w_s$, $R_1=w^s$, $L_2=u'_s$, $R_2=u'^s$ and the natural isomorphism $\delta^{-1}:u'^s\xrightarrow{\sim}w^s$ of Step 5 (uniqueness of adjoints, Categories, Lemma 0B65): there is a natural isomorphism $w_s\cong u'_s$.

*Step 7 ($u'_s$ is exact).* $w_s$ commutes with finite limits and finite colimits (Step 3). For a finite diagram in $\Sh(\mathcal A)$ with limit cone $\lambda$, the cone $u'_s(\lambda)$ is isomorphic, through the components of the isomorphism $w_s\cong u'_s$ of Step 6, to the limit cone $w_s(\lambda)$, and a cone isomorphic to a limit cone is a limit cone; dually for colimits. Hence $u'_s$ is exact, and with Step 4 the continuous functor $u'$ defines a morphism of sites $\mathcal B\to\mathcal A$ (Sites, Definition 00X1, [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology](3)).
